name: Coelophysis bauri
dietDetails: Preyed on small reptiles and cynodonts.
discoveryHistory: Discovered by E.D. Cope in 1887 in New Mexico.
interestingFacts: ["Early agile theropod.", "Mass bonebeds at Ghost Ranch.", "Hollow thin-walled bones."]
sources: [{"citation": "Cope, E.D. (1887). Trans. Amer. Phil. Soc.", "url": "https://doi.org/10.2307/1005527"}]

name: Plateosaurus trossingensis
dietDetails: High foliage, cycads, and conifers, processed with leaf-shaped teeth.
discoveryHistory: Discovered in 1834 near Nuremberg, Germany, by Johann Engelhardt. Described by Hermann von Meyer in 1837.
interestingFacts: {"An early sauropodomorph, a group that would eventually evolve into the giant, long-necked sauropods.","Strictly bipedal; its hands were unable to rotate, making quadrupedal walking anatomically impossible.","Fossil mass graves in Europe suggest they traveled in herds or became trapped in mud flats."}
sizeNotes: Highly variable adult sizes, ranging from 4.8 to 10 meters in length and 600 to 4,000 kg.
sources: [{"citation":"von Meyer, H. (1837). Original description of Plateosaurus trossingensis.","url":"https://paleobiodb.org/classic/basicTaxonInfo?taxon_no=38670"},{"citation":"Paleobiology Database (PBDB) species record","url":"https://paleobiodb.org"},{"citation":"Plateosaurus spp. description in paleontological literature","url":"https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plateosaurus"}]

interestingFacts: ["Superficially resembled a marine turtle but belonged to the extinct placodont order of sauropterygians.","Had two distinct protective carapace shields: one covering the shoulders/chest and a smaller one over the pelvis.","Possessed toothless, narrow beaked jaws lined internally with flat, pavement-like crushing plates."]
sizeNotes: Turtle-like marine placodont with a flattened, armored body split into two shields.
